title: How a rolling deploy keeps a site up
mechanism: Each server leaves the pool, takes the new version, passes its check and rejoins, one stage per tick, before the next one leaves.
claim: Only one server is ever out, so the site keeps two thirds of its capacity from the first tick to the last.
implication: A deploy takes longer the more servers there are, and never costs more than one of them.

beats.title: One leaves
beats.plain: The first server stops taking traffic, takes the new version, and is checked, a stage per tick.

beats.title: Back, then the next
beats.plain: It rejoins on the new version, and only then does the second server leave.

beats.title: The rest follow
beats.plain: The others go the same way, one behind the other, until every server runs the new version.
